first90Days.focus: Sponsor alignment, scope one domain, name stewards
activities: Verify sponsor budget authority; qualify out if absent
Draft, socialise and sign the DG charter
Place the council within the existing committee hierarchy
Agree the first domain and write the exclusions explicitly
Name Data Owners and secure written acceptance
Name stewards with a countersigned time percentage
Capture the benefit baseline before delivery starts
first90Days.exitArtefact: Signed charter, named and time-allocated roles, benefit baseline recorded

first90Days.focus: CDE identification via backward lineage from top reports
activities: Select the consumption points that define criticality
Identify the priority regulatory returns and their line items
Trace lineage backwards from each consumption point to source fields
Consolidate and de-duplicate into a draft CDE register
Rate criticality and assign owner and steward per element
Ratify the register at council and place it under change control
first90Days.exitArtefact: CDE register — typically 50–100 elements for a first domain — ratified and owned

first90Days.focus: Deploy catalogue, ingest metadata, build glossary
activities: Confirm the tooling decision and deploy the platform
Configure connectors; prove extraction from the vendor core
Schedule automated harvest with failure alerting
Populate the glossary for governed terms and resolve contested definitions
Bind every CDE to its physical columns
Capture lineage for the governed elements and classify each one
first90Days.exitArtefact: Live catalogue with glossary, binding, classification and lineage for the scoped domain

first90Days.focus: Author and run DQ rules on CDEs
activities: Profile the source systems and establish a defect baseline
Tailor rules from the library and agree thresholds with owners
Deploy rules to the engine and schedule execution
Stand up the scorecard layer over the result store
Publish the first scorecard and walk owners through their results
Enforce at least one policy as code in a pipeline
first90Days.exitArtefact: First DQ scorecard published — the artefact that funds the following six months

first90Days.focus: Issue workflow live, first council cycle, remediate top defects
activities: Open the issue queue and triage the first tranche of defects
Run the first full council cycle with recorded decisions
Remediate the five highest-severity defects and evidence the change
Measure defect-rate movement against the baseline
Assemble the derivation and lineage evidence pack
Scope the next domain using the same derivation method
first90Days.exitArtefact: Governance running with a measurable delta, and the next wave scoped

waves.name: Mobilise & Derive
waves.theme: Authority and scope. No technical build until the mandate and the element list exist.
objectives: Establish an authority base that survives the first cross-domain dispute
Convert the charter into named people with allocated time
Produce a finite, defensible CDE register derived from consumption
deliverables: Signed DG charter and constituted council
Ownership register with written acceptances
Steward allocation letters countersigned by line managers
Ratified CDE register with owners and criticality
Benefit baseline record
kpis: Percentage of CDEs with a named steward
waves.exitCriteria: Charter signed, stewards time-allocated, CDE register ratified at council. Gates G1–G6.
externalDependencies: Access to regulatory reporting and risk specialists

waves.name: Platform & Catalogue
waves.theme: Make the estate addressable. Catalogue, glossary, lineage and classification for the scoped domain.
objectives: Deploy the platform and prove extraction from the vendor core
Populate the glossary and bind every CDE to physical columns
Capture lineage end to end and classify every governed element
deliverables: Catalogue, quality engine and lineage collector running
Scheduled metadata harvest with failure alerting
Glossary populated with contested definitions resolved at council
CDE-to-column binding complete
Classification recorded against every governed CDE
waves.exitCriteria: Harvest running on schedule; every CDE has a definition, a binding, a lineage path and a classification.

waves.name: Quality & Scorecard
waves.theme: Make governance visible. Rules bound to CDEs, executing on schedule, published as a number the business recognises.
objectives: Establish a defect baseline through profiling
Deploy the rule set against every governed CDE
Publish a scorecard and get it reviewed at council
deliverables: Profiling baseline per source system
Deployed rule set with owner-agreed thresholds
Published DQ scorecard with a named owner per failing rule
Issue queue open and triaged by stewards
At least one policy enforced as code in a pipeline
waves.exitCriteria: Scorecard published and reviewed at council; issues being triaged by stewards rather than by the delivery team. Gate G8.

waves.name: Regulatory Defensibility
waves.theme: Convert lineage and quality into evidence a regulator or auditor will accept without a three-week investigation.
objectives: Complete return line-item to source-field lineage for the priority submissions
Automate reconciliation between GL, subledger and source
Assemble a maintained evidence pack
deliverables: Return line-item lineage for the priority submissions
Automated reconciliation controls with break ageing
Manual intervention and end-user-computing register with risk ratings
Regulator-presentable derivation evidence pack
Model and ECL input quality controls running pre-execution
kpis: Return line items with complete lineage
waves.exitCriteria: Derivation of any priority return line item can be evidenced on request from live lineage.

waves.name: Master Data & Single Customer View
waves.theme: Fix the entity resolution problem that silently breaks exposure aggregation, KYC currency and customer analytics.
objectives: Define and publish the golden customer record
Establish the stewardship queue for match exceptions
Make group and related-party aggregation reliable
deliverables: Golden record definition with survivorship rules
Match and merge rules keyed on validated national identifiers
Stewardship queue live for match exceptions
Group and related-party linkage register
Reference code-set register with named owners and change control
waves.exitCriteria: Group exposure can be aggregated on demand with evidenced completeness; duplicate rate trending down.

waves.name: AI & Consumption Readiness
waves.theme: Turn the governed estate into an AI-deployable one — the wedge that opened the engagement, now closed out.
objectives: Publish a certified dataset and report register
Install a data-readiness gate in the AI and analytics intake
Make model inputs traceable to governed elements
deliverables: Certified report and trusted dataset register
AI intake process with an enforced data-readiness gate
Model input traceability to governed CDEs
Classification and entitlement controls extended to the AI consumption layer
Shadow reporting inventory with a rationalisation plan
kpis: Use cases passing the readiness gate
waves.exitCriteria: An AI use case has passed the gate on evidence rather than assertion, with entitlements enforced at query time.

waves.name: Run, Prove & Expand
waves.theme: Prove the client can run a full cycle unaided, evidence the benefit, and onboard the next domain.
objectives: Demonstrate handover independence over a full cycle
Measure benefit against the pre-programme baseline
Scope and mobilise the next domain
deliverables: Full monthly cycle run by client staff with the delivery team observing
Benefit realisation report against baseline
Access recertification executed with exceptions closed
Next domain scope statement using the same derivation method
Transition into the managed governance retainer
waves.exitCriteria: Client-run cycle completed; benefit evidenced; next domain scoped. Gate G10.

builtFrom.note: The 55 weighted diagnostic questions, five per pillar, scored through scoring.ts with its three states. 55 of 55 question texts and 55 of 55 levelDescription blocks are distinct and the weight sequence carries no cycle at any period — the instrument is authored, not generated, which is the test HACR's nine template stems and five-cycle weight fail.

sourceSystem, domain, ownerRole and consumers, per element: 32 systems, 16 domains, 234 consumption points. 11 of the 53 reference-model entities are sourced by more than one system, and that irregularity is what a positional assignment could not produce. SYSTEM-TO-SYSTEM FLOWS ARE IN NO DATASET — the map is system to domain to consumption, one hop each. The ownership section is legitimately empty (0 of 76 owners unresolved) and must print the zero with its reason.

The client's own rework hours, findings and headcount, measured during the diagnostic. positioning holds pain as prose and no baseline exists anywhere. DGIW persists exactly one thing today — dgiw_diagnostic_answers — so there is no surface to record this in.

The seven waves with dependsOn, and the eleven gates through flow.gateIds. The wave-to-gate relation is prose inside wave.exitCriteria, parsed and labelled prose-derived on the page; it is not a foreign key and is not presented as one.

consumers, inverted. 3 to 5 entries per element over 234 distinct values, distribution 40x4 / 32x3 / 4x5 — non-periodic, and domain-coherent throughout (customer elements to eCIB and KYC, loan elements to ECL and repricing). This is the field where an HCF-LINK counter would live and it is not one. TWO AUTHORED HOPS ONLY: consumption point to element to source system. No transformation logic and no column-level detail exists anywhere — see AR-25, which is this same data with the boundary removed.

The five P11 questions with their level descriptions, the P11 pillar score and its three states, and the three P11 crosswalk entries. PILLAR LEVEL ONLY — no candidate use case exists in any dataset, so the ladder's 'per candidate use case' phrasing cannot be met. Where P11's focus names classification, traceability and quality as dependencies, P08, P07 and P05 print as separate scores; averaging them would be a rollup the data does not define.

BLOCKED, D5 stage G, previously buildable-looking. The 234 free-text consumers strings include SBP prudential returns, eCIB submission and capital adequacy, and keyword-classifying them into regulatory obligations yields a confident document with no join behind it — the TCF capability badge in a new module. No return, regulator, deadline or obligation register exists. AR-21 supplies the relation.

RE-DISPOSITIONED from derived to authored, Wave B. A charter is a TEMPLATE filled per engagement, not a document derived from a dataset, and positioning.accelerators says so itself — it advertises a 'templated charter' in the same sentence as the policy set and the issue workflow, both already authored here. What makes a charter a charter is absent from every dataset: a scope statement with explicit exclusions (checklist CL-05 catalogues that separately), a term, an amendment procedure, a review cycle and a signature block. operatingModel.council.charterPurpose is not the missing mandate — read it, it is a COUNCIL purpose, 'to hold decision rights over enterprise data at a level below the executive committee'. Everything else a charter would draw on — the seven principles, the ten roles, the council object — is already rendered by AR-09, so a generator here would assemble AR-09's content under a cover saying Charter. That is the AR-46 shape, matching the shape and nothing else. Marking it derived in D5 stage G was an error against AR-11 and AR-16; this corrects it. Author the template, then a generator can fill it.

The declared 15-activity by 5-role RACI, the 32-entry role registry that resolves free-text owners to archetypes, the seven delivery flows with their steps, and the 52-item checklist. checklist.phase and flow.name are NOT joined — they resemble each other and are not equal, and the report states that rather than inventing the mapping.

artefactRegister.artefact: Council terms of reference and decision rights

builtFrom.note: WITHDRAWN, Wave B. Not because the data cannot support it — it is the most literal match in the register — but because it is ALREADY DELIVERED. report/operatingModel.ts renders a Data Governance Council page carrying all seven fields of operatingModel.council: charterPurpose, chair, cadence, quorum, members, decisionRights, escalationPath. Nothing is held back for a second document to add. Measured before deciding: the only content a standalone terms of reference could add is the council's own rows of the RACI (accountable on 3 of 15 activities, consulted on 4), one table; and member archetype resolution is NOT available, because 0 of the 8 members resolve through roleRegistry — they are role descriptions ('Risk representative'), not registry titles. Two documents over seven identical fields is one operating model under two covers, and cataloguing it twice is how a register grows a duplicate — the test that withdrew AR-34. REVERSIBLE with a stated trigger: re-catalogue it if the council object gains what distinguishes a maintained instrument from a snapshot (a version, a review date, an amendment record), or if AR-09's council page is ever replaced by a cross-reference, at which point the terms of reference has somewhere of its own to live.

NO POLICY SET EXISTS IN ANY DATASET. positioning.accelerators advertises a library of 'templated charter, policy set, RACI, issue workflow, council terms of reference and phase-gate checklist' — the charter, RACI, terms of reference and checklist are in operatingModel.json and programSetup.json; the policy set and the issue workflow are not. Eight to twelve policies: the largest single authoring gap in this register.
The mapping needs the policies. Gate G7 and step F4-S3 both name this exact output and there is no policy set to map to an enforcement point.

76 elements with the owner string resolved to an archetype through roles.ts, joined to the rules in scope under the active layer. 0 of 76 owner strings are unresolved; the column still prints UNRESOLVED rather than a blank if one ever is. THE OPEN-RISK LOG IS THIS ENTRY, NOT A SEPARATE ONE: step F3-S5 produces 'Open-risk log for unassigned elements', CL-20 names it, and gate G5 requires that unassigned elements are recorded as open risks rather than silently carried — all three are the UNRESOLVED rows of this register, which is empty today and is a state of the same artefact rather than a second one. Catalogued here rather than given an id of its own.

RENAMED from 'System-of-record map', D5 stage G. fsdmEntity groups the 76 elements into 53 entities: 11 are sourced by more than one system, 42 by exactly one. NEITHER IS A DESIGNATION. No designation field exists, and one system appearing without a competitor is the absence of a second row, not a decision — that is the difference between a foreign key resolving and a relation being real. The register reports the three states as a work list for the Data Architect and must never name a system of record. CL-21 CARRIED THE OLD NAME UNTIL NOW: it asked for a 'System-of-record map' and asserted 'system of record designated for each CDE', which is the shape this rename removed and at the wrong grain besides — designation is per fsdmEntity, of which there are 53, not per element. It now names this register and states the designation as the Data Owner's decision.

Labels and handling rules, authored once. criticality is CRITICAL or HIGH — business impact, not confidentiality — and labelling elements from it would be the two-vocabularies error at the level of the value rather than the join.
States, transitions and an SLA per severity. Gate G9 and the RACI both reference a triage SLA that is specified nowhere in the repo. council.escalationPath supplies the escalation half.

positioning.toolingTiers — two tiers, eight components with product and selection note — P10's constraints, deliverables and overlay artefacts, and the 32 source systems from the CDE register as the connector scope. NO INTEGRATION EDGES AND NO DEPLOYMENT TOPOLOGY EXIST: P10 names an on-premise topology as an artefact without containing one, so the diagram is capability layers, not a wired architecture. First generator to read positioning.json, which is screen-only today.

Costs, benefits and payback measured at the client. The phased-plan half is AR-04 and is already generated; the case half has no source, and a plausible ROI assembled beside a real roadmap is the most inviting fabrication in this register.
Statutory periods per record category with legal basis. One element carries fsdmEntity 'Retention Rule', which records that retention rules are data — not what any of them say.

fsdmEntity: 53 reference-model entities over 76 elements, semantically matched to their element names and irregularly distributed. REVERSE COVERAGE IS NOT COMPUTABLE — the reference model's own catalogue is not in this repo, so which of its entities nothing maps cannot be stated and must not be implied by a coverage percentage.

Return line items traced to source fields, per submission. Named as an accelerator, carried by no dataset. It is the missing input for AR-07, AR-38 and AR-45 as well as for itself, which makes it the highest-leverage authoring item in the banking overlay.
The artefact is a running platform. The 32 source systems in the CDE register scope the connectors; the harvest, the coverage and the schedule are client runtime.

element, definition, domain and resolved owner: 76 authored definitions averaging some 200 characters and bound to their element. No synonyms, no approval status and no physical binding exist — the glossary is unapproved and says so on the page. Same rows as AR-13 under a business-term cut, not a second body of evidence.

BLOCKED, D5 stage G, previously buildable-looking. The apparent path is parsing physical identifiers out of dqRules.expression — cif_no, gl_account, cost_centre. Expressions reference several columns, joins and subqueries, and one element carries rules naming different columns, so selecting THE column is a guess. The binding is an output of the catalogue's harvest.

BLOCKED, D5 stage G, previously buildable-looking. sourceSystem and consumers are two authored endpoints with nothing between them; a lineage graph built from them means inventing the hops. AR-05 is the honest rung-1 version of this same data, and the difference between the two entries is one boundary sentence. Middle hops come from the lineage collector, never from inference.
Profiling results per source system. The rules and their thresholds exist; the defect counts do not, and inventing them is how a baseline stops being a baseline.
115 rules with expression, threshold, severity and remediation, joined to the element each protects. A rule whose element is out of scope under the active layer is flagged, never dropped.
Rule execution results. 115 rules with thresholds, severities and owners are in the dataset and only the pass rates are missing — which is precisely what makes filling them in easy and wrong.
Issues raised, triaged and closed against the SLA that AR-16 has to define first.
The artefact is an enforced pipeline gate, not a document. Gate G7 requires one enforcement point per policy; the enforcement itself runs in the client's pipeline.
Spreadsheets and hand adjustments found during the engagement. Nothing in this repo describes a manual touchpoint, and a risk-rated register of them is discovery output.

Re-catalogue it when survivorship is authored, not before.

BLOCKED, D5 stage G, previously buildable-looking. The apparent path is a regex over dqRules.expression, which yields nine ref_* table names and five inline enums and looks like a code-set register. It carries no code values, no owner, no versioning and no change process — which is the entire content of the artefact. P06 IS THE LEAST-INSTRUMENTED PILLAR IN THE MODULE AND THIS ENTRY IS HALF OF THE EVIDENCE: P06 Master & Reference Data holds 0 of the 52 checklist items, has no built artefact, and its only two register entries are this one and AR-32, which is withdrawn — while waves W2 and W4 both name it. Every other pillar carries at least one checklist item. Visible only by reading the sequence against the register, which is why it is recorded here rather than left to be noticed.

WITHDRAWN, D5 stage G. Two halves and neither survives. The derivable half — the consumption-point inventory — is already AR-02's third section, and cataloguing it twice is how a register grows a duplicate. The other half is certification, a council decision recorded nowhere: consumption is not certification, and the consumers strings are unnormalised besides (eCIB and eCIB submission are one return). DG-P11-01 asks the client whether they hold such a register; it does not produce one.

AR-27's generator under layer=banking: 75 of 115 rules across CIF & Party, Deposits & Accounts, Loans & Advances, Cards, Collateral, GL & Finance and Treasury. ONE GENERATOR, TWO CATALOGUE ENTRIES — wire this id to the existing builder; do not write a second.

THE SEQUENCE ASKED FOR IT ANYWAY UNTIL NOW: checklist item CL-40 was a BLOCKING banking item named 'Reconciliation rule set', requiring 'reconciliation controls between GL, subledger and source automated' — a consultant would have been blocked on an artefact this entry records as unbuildable. The register was dispositioned top-down in D5 stage G and the sequence was not read against it; that is the gap ARTEFACT-SEQUENCE is proposed to close.

builtFrom.note: The four published frameworks, the 91 crosswalk entries with their authored rationale, and the pillar scores the projection consumes. Leaf dimensions only: a dimension with children carries no entries and rolls up inside its framework, never across the pillar side.

The same projection as AR-47 across all four frameworks side by side, with each framework's weakest three dimensions and the pillars it maps nothing to. Scales differ per framework and are rescaled explicitly rather than printed under one another's heading.

CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE, not from the ladder: step F4-S5 produces it and CL-28 requires it with a time-limiting rule on every exception, and no register entry existed for either. The content is council decisions granted during the engagement, which is AR-29's shape exactly — a runtime log measured against an authored definition. It cannot be opened before AR-11 exists, because an exception is an exception TO a policy; that dependency is stated here rather than as blockedOn, since what is missing is the content to record, not a buildable input.

CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-30 names it and nothing carried it. A constraint per element is a Compliance determination made from the client's own legal position, not library content. THE APPARENT PATH IS CDE-010 'Customer Residency & Domicile' and CDE-061 'Party Address' — elements ABOUT residency and jurisdiction, which is not the same as a transfer or confidentiality constraint attached to an element, exactly as AR-19's 'Retention Rule' entity records that retention rules are data without recording what any of them say. The confidentiality half additionally needs AR-15's label vocabulary before it can be written down consistently.

CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-36 requires it as a blocking Platform item and P07's own coreArtefacts names 'Lineage coverage metric against governed CDEs'; no entry existed. The denominator is in the repo — the governed CDEs under the active layer — and the numerator is what the collector actually harvested, which AR-25 records comes from the lineage collector and never from inference. AR-28's shape: everything but the measured half is present, which is what makes filling it in easy and wrong.

CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-37 requires classification applied and recorded against every governed CDE, as a blocking Platform item, and no entry existed. Genuinely derivable once AR-15's labels exist and are attached — the denominator is already the governed CDE set under the layer filter and the three states apply unchanged, labelled / not-labelled / not-applicable, never a zero. It must NOT be derived from cdeRegister.criticality: CRITICAL and HIGH are business impact, not confidentiality, which is the two-vocabularies error at the level of the value that AR-15's own note fences off.

artefactRegister.artefact: Model and ECL input control set

builtFrom.note: CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-45 asks for model and ECL input checks running before model execution, and no entry existed. 'Running before model execution' is a runtime property of the client's pipeline, as AR-30 is. THE APPARENT PATH IS THE CONSUMPTION POINT 'ECL computation', which is the highest-ranked point in the register at six feeding elements, joined to their DQ rules — refused because consumers is free text and unnormalised, no model inventory exists to say which models these are or who owns them, and AR-06 established that no candidate use case exists in any dataset. A control set assembled from a consumption-point string would be the AR-07 bridge with a model risk heading.

THE INVERSE OF A COVERAGE REPORT, WHICH IS NOT BUILDABLE. Per pillar: the checklist items and register entries filed against it, every entry with its disposition, and each framework's induced share from the projection engine — four columns, never summed, because leaf weights total 1.00 in DMBOK2 and 3.00 in DGI. Three states, and NOT CATALOGUED never renders as zero. NO DATASET RELATES A CHECKLIST ITEM OR AN ARTEFACT TO A FRAMEWORK DIMENSION: the pillarId on those two is a filing with no weight and no rationale, where the crosswalk entry carries both, so no coverage figure appears anywhere. Waves are reported wave-to-pillar only; artefact-to-wave is a string bridge, 1 of 35 deliverable strings matching a register name.
